The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for many shoppers
Why, in plain words: An administrator switched on a new feature for the account page, and it likely sent shoppers who had bought nothing this month through a calculation that divides by their number of purchases this month, which fails when that number is zero.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 38.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,182.30 USD {customer_loss}
- People who responded: 2 {responders}
- Their time, added together: 17 min {engineer_minutes}
- What their time cost: {responder_cost} (its amount is not shown to you; name it where it goes)

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #527 - opened as a draft

Name {duration}, {customer_loss} and {responder_cost} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for many shoppers while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:02 to 02:10 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:33:39 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:08:38 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 02:02 UTC and was back to normal at 02:10 UTC, 8 minutes later. 26.9% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 38.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,182.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. An administrator switched on a new feature for the account page, and it likely sent shoppers who had bought nothing this month through a calculation that divides by their number of purchases this month, which fails when that number is zero. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #527, for a person to review and merge. Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could again fail account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month, and by Code-Fix's reading, the account page can still fail with the flag off for an account with no purchases at all.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
38.5% - peak error rate
2,580 - requests failed
1.0% to 26.9% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,182.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary goes through `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases marked as this month's, and has no case for a shopper who has bought before but not this month: for that shopper the count is zero and the division raises ZeroDivisionError. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 occurrences in 9 minutes, 02:00–02:08; # was 0.50% to 38.50%, typically 28.00%, highest at 02:03
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:02–02:08
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, at the line the log names. This error started in the minute the flag was switched on and kept going until the log lines that were read end.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 The account page reached that code because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at 02:02:28 UTC. The page's flag evaluations were all off over 02:00–02:01 UTC, split between off and on in 02:02 UTC, and all on over 02:03–02:08 UTC.
  Evidence:
    P1 02:02:28 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:00–02:01
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 / on 102 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:02
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:03–02:08
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 02:03; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    Another flag change. The flag provider's history showed no other flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before it was read.
      T14 02:09:08 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:09:08
      P1
why 3 With the flag on, the account page's figure is computed by dividing the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- When monthly-spend-feature was switched on, it reached the account page's whole traffic within the minute after the change. No staged rollout, or check of the error rate on a small share of traffic, was seen before that. (AI-3)
- No test was seen that exercises the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has no purchases this month. By Code-Fix's reading, the existing tests in the files it read expect the flag-off path's error for an account with no purchases at all. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 02:02:28 UTC. That enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 30%. No deployment was involved. | 0.95 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 02:02:28 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:09:23 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 02:12:39 | Proposed a fix: PR #527 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:02 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 02:08:12 UTC, 6 minutes 12 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #527 | open
AI-3 | Roll out feature flag switch-ons in production to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the service's error rate stays at its usual level. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Require tests that exercise the code path a feature flag turns on, including shoppers with no purchases in the period it covers, before that flag can be switched on in production. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Decide whether `average_spend_per_item`, used with the flag off, should still raise for an account with no purchases at all, which the current tests expect. If it should not, fix it. | prevent | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 56 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 11 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 2 minutes 50 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 27 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #527.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 11 02:02 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 02:08:12 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 02:08:33 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop

T6 | 02:09:04 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 02:09:05 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 02:03

T17 | 02:09:30 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 02:10 - up to 156s

Response effort
17 min - engineer time, 2 responders (Senior Software Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer)
153,813 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/b2d5cbb0-ad0a-4f85-a40a-f7570736b94e
The fix it proposed: PR #527 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/527) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 02:02:28 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:00–02:01
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 3 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:00–02:01
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 9 occurrences in 9 minutes, 02:00–02:08; # was 0.50% to 38.50%, typically 28.00%, highest at 02:03
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 98 / on 102 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:02
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:02–02:08
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:03–02:08
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides account.total_this_month_cents by len(bought_this_month), the number of purchases flagged in_current_month. Most shoppers have bought before but not this month. For them that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. That is the line the incident log names (spend_summary.py:47). Turning on monthly-spend-feature sent the account page's figure through this function, and every request for such a shopper failed.

The flag was what triggered the incident, but the fault is in the code: the function has no answer for the normal case of a shopper who has bought nothing this month. With the fix, when there are no purchases this month the function returns 0, because a shopper with no purchases this month has spent nothing this month. Otherwise it divides as before. Shoppers who did buy this month get the same result as before.

Other code is unchanged. With the flag off, render_spend_summary still uses average_spend_per_item, and that function still raises for an account with no purchases at all. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py expect that error, and that error is the only case the line-number test in test_account_page.py checks. Nothing in this change catches errors.

The tests: the new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py call average_spend_per_item_this_month and render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for a shopper whose purchases all fall outside the current month, and assert 0. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, account pages failed for some shoppers for {duration}. An administrator switched on a new feature for the account page. It likely sent shoppers who had bought nothing this month through a calculation that divides by their number of purchases this month, and that calculation fails when the number is zero. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. {responders} people responded and spent {engineer_minutes} on it in total, which cost {responder_cost}. Argus ended the incident by turning off the feature flag monthly-spend-feature. That change is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix, PR #527. It is still a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
